HO00007487.title: DocHouse: American Doctor
HO00007487.description:
This timely film follows three doctors from very different backgrounds who travel to Gaza to volunteer in hospitals overwhelmed by war. 

Working amid bombardment, severe medical shortages and constant danger, the three doctors - Palestinian American emergency physician Thaer Ahmad, Jewish American orthopedic surgeon Mark Perlmutter and Zoroastrian trauma surgeon Feroze Sidhwa - bear witness to the devastating impact of the conflict on Gaza's hospitals in particular. 

When they return, they are compelled to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines to the halls of Congress, and challenging prevailing media narrative from their first hand position.

Filmed on the ground in Gaza and back in the US, AMERICAN DOCTOR is a deeply human portrait of courage, compassion and moral responsibility.

HO00006864.title: DocHouse: Everybody to Kenmure St.
HO00006864.description: Glasgow residents abandon their daily routines to gather on Kenmure Street after learning authorities plan to deport their neighbors.

HO00007533.title: DocHouse: Harlan County USA
HO00007533.description:
Barbara Kopple’s Academy Award–winning HARLAN COUNTY USA (1976) unflinchingly documents a gruelling coal miners’ strike in a small Kentucky town.
With unprecedented access, Kopple and her crew captured the miners’ sometimes violent struggles with strikebreakers, local police and company thugs.

Featuring a haunting soundtrack - with legendary country and bluegrass artists Hazel Dickens, Merle Travis, Sarah Gunning and Florence Reece - the film is a heartbreaking record of the thirteen-month struggle between a community fighting to survive and a corporation dedicated to the bottom line.

HO00007230.title: DocHouse: How to Feed a Dictator
HO00007230.description:
This film tells the story of five brutal regimes, from Iraq to North Korea, through the eyes of the personal chefs who served them.

Through recipes, rituals and remembrance, a portrait emerges of power, manipulation and the quiet ways ordinary people become entangled in extraordinary violence. Loyalty, denial, fear, even thrill, each chef carries their experience differently, yet together they reveal how dictatorship gets under the skin of everyone it touches. HOW TO FEED A DICTATOR is darkly funny, deeply human and impossible to shake, proof that the most revealing place to understand a regime is not the war room but the kitchen.

HO00006777.title: DocHouse: It's Never Over, Jeff Buckley
HO00006777.description:
IT’S NEVER OVER, JEFF BUCKLEY, directed by Oscar-nominated filmmaker Amy Berg, covers the life of the rising young star with an otherworldly voice and boundary-pushing artistry, who left the '90s music world reeling when he died suddenly, at age 30, after the release of his critically acclaimed debut album “Grace.”

Told through never-before-seen footage from Buckley’s archives and intimate accounts from his mother Mary Guibert, former partners Rebecca Moore and Joan Wasser, Jeff’s former bandmates, including Michael Tighe and Parker Kindred, and luminaries like Ben Harper and Aimee Mann, IT’S NEVER OVER, JEFF BUCKLEY illuminates one of modern music’s most influential and enigmatic figures.

HO00007488.title: DocHouse: LDNDOCS: To Hold a Mountain
HO00007488.description:
In the remote highlands of Montenegro, a shepherd and her teenage daughter hold on to a traditional rural lifestyle amid the growing pressures of the contemporary world.

Gara passes on her wealth of ancestral knowledge to Nada, as they herd animals, gather herbs, make cheese and live in symbiosis with the mountain and their community.

As Gara fights to defend their home from the threat of becoming a NATO military training ground, Nada must begin to think about her own future, as the pain of their family history is slowly revealed.

Winner of this year's Sundance World Documentary prize, TO HOLD A MOUNTAIN is a film rich in gently observed details, from the demands of pastoral labour to the love in domestic rituals.

HO00007532.title: DocHouse: Made of Truth: Common Ground
HO00007532.description:
BFI Doc Society presents a selection of recent short documentaries funded through the Made of Truth fund.

Our relationships with each other are continuous and dynamic - we shape our communities and our communities shape us. This programme of short-but-perfectly-formed-docs explores individuals and their communities and the social threads that lie within and unite us. 

From a women's group in Belfast crafting a performance from their shared experiences of addiction to a story of displacement in the olive groves of southeast Turkey, a South Asian cavalry sport being played with vigour in Bradford, and the radical impact of two sisters in a Pembrokeshire village, this programme explores the many different meanings of community, whether forged by location, by conflict, by shared passion or by common ground.

HO00007476.title: DocHouse: Maverick: Epic Adventures of David Lean
HO00007476.description:
David Lean was one of the greatest film directors of all time. From Brief Encounter (1945) to Lawrence of Arabia (1962) to A Passage to India (1984) and so many more, he redefined what movies could be: he was both  pioneer of the  large-scale epic and the master of the intimate romantic drama. 

Lean's singular vision and dogged determination to film the impossible gained him the reputation of being an obsessive maverick. He was a master of his art, able to create love and beauty on screen, but whose own life was often messy, rootless and painful.

MAVERICK is the in-depth study of the man and his films, narrated by Cate Blanchett, with Kenneth Branagh is the voice of Lean, and featuring interviews with Wes Anderson,  Alfonso Cuaron, Celine Song, Denis Villeneuve, Nia DaCosta and Francis Ford Coppola.

HO00007547.title: DocHouse: Nova '78
HO00007547.description:
A cinematic time capsule from 1970s New York, NOVA '78 resurrects William S. Burroughs' legendary Nova Convention, which brought together some of the most celebrated and uncompromising artistic voices of the time.

Never-before-seen footage captures Burroughs along with icons such as Patti Smith, Frank Zappa, Laurie Anderson, Merce Cunningham, Allen Gisberrg, John Cage and many more, meeting in an electrifying artistic clash of readings, concerts and performances.

HO00007504.title: DocHouse: Nuisance Bear
HO00007504.description:
A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life.

For thousands of years, polar bears have migrated along the shores of Hudson Bay in northern Canada. Today, that ancient rhythm collides with a human world of tourism, surveillance and control. Shot with striking intimacy and scale, NUISANCE BEAR immerses viewers in the experience of a bear pushed into contact with the human world through development and climate change.

In tracing this uneasy new coexistence, the film overturns the conventions of the nature documentary and reframes animals not as spectacle, but as active agents in a rapidly changing world.

When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

HO00007523.title: DocHouse: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
HO00007523.description:
A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

HO00006879.title: DocHouse: Orwell: 2+2=5
HO00006879.description:
1949. George Orwell termine ce qui sera son dernier mais plus important roman, 1984.
ORWELL : 2+2=5 plonge dans les derniers mois de la vie d’Orwell et dans son œuvre.

HO00007570.title: DocHouse: Rehearsals for a Revolution
HO00007570.description:
Through five compelling portraits of people close to her heart, five expressions of resistance, Iranian filmmaker and actor Pegah Ahangarani sketches her life story, and the story of Iran.

Drawing from personal archives, home videos, street protest footage, newspaper reports and recorded voices, she retraces more than 40 years of Iran’s history.

From the early days of revolution in 1979, which her courageous father documented on 8mm film, through to her own recordings of the protests in 2009, and raw footage of the war that began in 2026, Ahangarani pieces together intimate and collective memories, forming the portrait of a country shaped by political repression and in constant hope for a revolution.

HO00007170.title: DocHouse: Replica
HO00007170.description:
In China, increasing numbers of young women are embarking on AI relationships. REPLICA follows three women whose virtual boyfriends fill emotional gaps left by loneliness, unfulfilling marriages and the pursuit of independence.

Qin, Muna and Sonya all have different reasons for finding AI love. For factory worker Qin, its more accessible than a real world relationship, whereas for young mum Muna, it provides the compassion and support missing from her marriage, and tech-savvy Sonya treats her AI lover as an emotional experiment - until it betrays her expectations. 

As their virtual relationships deepen, REPLICA reveals the fragile boundary between emotional freedom and reliance on AI, and explores how AI reshapes love, intimacy, and gender in modern China.

HO00007294.title: DocHouse: Shorts: Maybe Tomorrow + Allies in Exile
HO00007294.description:
This double bill of short films from exceptional Syrian filmmakers brings together stories of the bonds of friendship, displacement, loss and endurance during Assad's regime and in the precarious time since its sudden end.

MAYBE TOMORROW, directed by Wafa Mustafa and Waad Al-Kateab (FOR SAMA) follows Wafa's long search for her father, who was disappeared under Assad's regime. In ALLIES IN EXILE, filmmakers and friends Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al Halabi turn from documenting the frontlines of a revolution to filming the bureaucracy of exile whilst housed in a UK asylum hotel.

HO00007254.title: DocHouse: Steal This Story, Please!
HO00007254.description: Fiercely independent journalist Amy Goodman has spent three decades holding the powerful to account, reporting from war zones and the Democracy Now! newsroom. In STEAL THIS STORY, PLEASE!  Oscar-nominated filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin craft a riveting portrait of journalism’s power – and peril – in an era of corporate control and political attacks on truth.

HO00007571.title: DocHouse: The Archivist
HO00007571.description:
David "Doc" Rowe has spent decades documenting Britain's vibrant folk traditions. Now, with time running short, he faces a race to preserve his legacy.

Rowe has devoted his life to documenting customs, songs and celebrations that few others thought worthy of attention, building an extraordinary archive along the way. As personal challenges mount and the collection's future grows uncertain, the urgency of his mission sharpens. With remarkable access, we get close to Rowe as he pushes forward, idiosyncratic and unflappable, navigating the fragile line between preserving memory and letting go.

THE ARCHIVIST is a story about one person's determination to celebrate the living traditions that connect us to where we come from and who we are, whatever the cost.

HO00007322.title: DocHouse: The Cycle Of Love
HO00007322.description:
In 1977, PK, a young street artist from Delhi, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile journey to find the woman who had captured his heart.

Growing up poor and 'untouchable', young PK had to reckon with the caste system and with his own sense of self-worth, as he met fellow travellers and locals from all walks of life on his journey across the world. Oscar-nominated director Orlando von Einsiedel retraces PK's journey from India to Sweden in an extraordinarily uplifting film, that is not just about what can happen when you follow your heart, but is also a paean to the joy of chance encounters and the kindness of strangers.

HO00007546.title: DocHouse: The History of Concrete
HO00007546.description:
Following the finale of his TV series, filmmaker John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world's most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter.
To tell this seemingly drab story, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to increase his movie's appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble – literally and figuratively – as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

HO00007545.title: DocHouse: The Siege of Paradise
HO00007545.description:
With its turquoise seas, pastel-coloured cliffside houses and picture-perfect vibes, Italy's Cinque Terre is paradise on earth. Or it seems to be, for the four million tourists who descend on the area each summer.

Filmmaker Gar O'Rourke joins the throngs across one chaotic season, capturing beleaguered locals,  philosophical business owners,  harried visitors and expectant influencers. 

With an affectionate gaze and a sharp eye for detail, O'Rourke (SANATORIUM) reveals a very comical and surprisingly tender story of paradise under pressure, in the age of social-media driven tourism.

HO00006874.title: DocHouse: Trains
HO00006874.description:
Elegantly crafted entirely from black and white archive footage, TRAINS is a mesmerising portrait of Europe in the first half of the 20th Century. Taking in all the delights of early locomotive travel, the development of industry and commuter moments both unusual and mundane, the footage takes a darker turn as first one war and then another make their mark upon history and humanity.

Maciej Drygas' wordless documentary  - which won the IDFA Grand Prize - is a profound, sweeping history of the 20th Century, movingly capturing its hope and its tragedy.

HO00007522.title: DocHouse: Tutu
HO00007522.description:
One of the world's most beloved figures, Desmond Tutu was more than an Archbishop, he was a moral compass and a fearless champion of justice.

Director Sam Pollard crafts an incisive portrait of the rebel Archbishop who helped end Apartheid, tracing his active political life and interviewing friends and close companions to understand the man behind the impish laugh.

In the face of brutality, he stood resolute: a man of principles and steely determination, guided by fervent humanitarian principles and driven by his belief in the transformative power of forgiveness.

HO00007534.title: DocHouse: Union Town
HO00007534.description:
After 50 years documenting the battle for labour rights, Barbara Kopple's latest film follows delivery industry workers in New York as they take on some of the world's most powerful corporations, fighting for basic rights and fair wages. 

Completing her trilogy of documentaries that began with HARLAN COUNTY USA (1976) and AMERICAN DREAM (1990) - both Best Documentary Oscar winners - UNION TOWN interweaves the struggles of three distinct but related groups of workers - at UPS, Amazon and the massive app-based bike delivery workforce that New York, like so many cities globally, has become reliant on. 

Filmed in Kopple's intimate, verité style, UNION TOWN reveals a massive, vulnerable workforce propping up enormously profitable corporations, and the union teams organising and negotiating in the middle. An essential insight into the fabric of society in 2026.

HO00007505.title: DocHouse: Whispers in the Woods
HO00007505.description:
Delving deep into the woodland realms of the Vosges mountains, where lynxes, bears, deer, owls, capercaillies and other creatures roam, French wildlife photographer Vincent Munier seeks to capture the forest’s poetic sounds and pay tribute to the visual splendour of nature.

Travelling with his bird-watching father, who inspired the love of nature in him, and his own son, to whom he passes it on, Munier's latest film is a heartfelt appreciation of the untamed beauty of the natural world and its creatures.

HO00007489.title: DocHouse: You Can See Everything

From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING.
